films.title: Coward
films.funding: Lukas Dhont's third feature is led by his Belgian company The Reunion, with Lumen (France), Topkapi Films (Netherlands) and Versus (Belgium) as co-producers. Brussels' regional fund put in €125,000, which it lists as about 1.2% of the budget, so the film cost roughly €10 million. The Match Factory sells it abroad and Diaphana releases it in France.

films.title: Digger
films.funding: A Hollywood studio picture: Legendary Pictures produced it in partnership with Warner Bros., which also distributes it. Tom Cruise is a producer alongside Iñárritu and Mary Parent. Warner Bros. says the budget stayed at $125 million; reports of $160–180 million were denied by the studio.

films.title: The Social Reckoning
films.funding: Made by Sony's Columbia Pictures with Alcon Entertainment and released worldwide by Sony Pictures. The reported budget is $30–42 million, modest for a studio film with this cast.

films.title: Primetime
films.funding: A24 both finances and distributes this one. Robert Pattinson produces through his company Icki Eneo Arlo, with Range Media Partners and Square Peg also credited. No budget has been published.

films.title: The Invite
films.funding: Produced by Megan Ellison's Annapurna, then sold at Sundance 2026. A24 won a days-long bidding war against Focus Features and paid more than $12 million for the rights.

films.title: Sense and Sensibility
films.funding: Working Title Films produced it with November Pictures and Kiddo Films. Working Title belongs to Universal, which releases the film internationally while its arthouse label Focus Features handles the US.

films.title: Garance
films.funding: Produced in France by Chi-Fou-Mi Productions and Trésor Films, with Belgium's Artémis Productions as the foreign partner. StudioCanal distributes it in France and sells it internationally.

films.title: L'Espèce explosive
films.funding: A debut feature produced by 5à7 Films and built on public money. The Grand Est region backed it first, and France's CNC gave writing aid, an advance on receipts, music aid and distribution aid. The director says the CNC advance, won on the third try, unlocked the rest of the financing.

films.title: The Last One for the Road
match: The Last One for the Road
The Last One for the Road (Andiamo a bere l'ultima)
films.funding: Original title Le città di pianura. Vivo Film produced it with Germany's Maze Pictures and Rai Cinema, the film arm of Italy's public broadcaster. Italy's culture ministry and the Council of Europe fund Eurimages also contributed.

films.title: Naza
films.funding: A documentary from the No Other Land team, produced by James Wilson's JW Films with The Guardian, in association with Placeholder Films and Unseen Hand. Jonathan Glazer is an executive producer and mk2 Films handles world sales.

films.title: Notre salut
films.funding: A Franco-Belgian co-production by Kidam and Brussels-based Michigan Films, made for under €5 million. Co-producers include France 2 Cinéma, Belgium's public broadcaster RTBF and Be tv/Proximus, and the CNC gave an advance on receipts plus development and distribution aid.

films.title: Rose
films.funding: An Austrian-German co-production by Schubert, ROW Pictures and Walker & Worm Film. The Match Factory sells it, and the streamer Mubi bought it for North and Latin America, the UK, Italy and other territories.

films.title: Tegenwoordig heet iedereen sorry
films.funding: A Flemish youth film produced by Ivy Vanhaecke at deMENSEN, with Germany's CALA Filmproduktion and Juliet at Pupkin. LevelK sells it abroad. The listing we found names no public funds.

films.title: Franz
films.funding: A Kafka biopic stitched together from many public sources. Marlene Film (Prague), X Filme (Berlin) and Metro Films (Warsaw) produced it, joined by Czech, Polish and German broadcasters and Canal+. Funding came from Eurimages, the Czech Audiovisual Fund, the Polish Film Institute, Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg and Germany's DFFF.

films.title: Mémoire de fille
films.funding: Judith Godrèche's adaptation of Annie Ernaux is produced by Windy Production. Paradise City Sales handles international sales and Jour2Fête releases it in France.

films.title: Minotaur
films.funding: A French-German-Latvian co-production led by MK Productions and CG Cinema, with Forma Pro Films, Razor Film and ARTE France Cinéma. mk2 Films sells it and Les Films du Losange distributes it; France picked it as its Oscar entry.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.funding: Universal Pictures financed and distributes it, produced with Nolan and Emma Thomas's company Syncopy. At about $250 million it is one of Nolan's most expensive films. Studio Skoop shows it on 35mm.

films.title: Dune: Part Three
films.funding: Legendary Entertainment and Warner Bros. produce it, as with the first two parts, and it was shot at Origo Studios in Hungary. No budget has been published.

films.title: Wicker
films.funding: Financed by Tango and Topic Studios, with development money from Votiv; South of The River and Yoki also produce. Black Bear bought it at Sundance 2026 for North America and the UK and handles international sales.

films.title: The Golden Spurtle
films.funding: A small documentary produced by Hytra Films in Australia, with development and production support from the public agency Screen Australia.

films.title: Yugly
films.funding: Brussels animation studio nWave made it with Octopolis. The Belgian tax shelter, raised through Umedia, and screen.brussels helped pay for it. Shown as Mochy in French.

films.title: Born in the Jungle
films.funding: A Latvian-Polish-Czech animation by Atom Art, Letko and Hausboot. Shown as Magische Jungle at Studio Skoop. Sources we found name no funders.

films.title: La Grande rêvasion
films.funding: A 45-minute animation made for television by Autour de Minuit and Kwassa Films, co-produced by Canal+. It won the Annecy Cristal for TV production.

films.title: The Pout-Pout Fish
films.funding: An independently financed animation made for under $10 million by MIMO Studios, Like a Photon Creative, Cosmic Dino Studio, Alceon Entertainment and Eclectik Vision.

films.title: Shaun het Schaap: Het Beest op de Boerderij
match: Shaun het Schaap: Het Beest op de Boerderij
Shaun Het Schaap: Het Beest van de Boerderij
Shaun het Schaap: het beest van de boerderij
films.funding: Aardman made it as a Sky Original: Sky releases it in the UK and StudioCanal everywhere else. Original title The Beast of Mossy Bottom.

films.title: The Devils (1971)
films.funding: Warner Bros. financed Ken Russell's film through Russo Productions and then cut it heavily for release. The new 4K restoration brings back material the studio removed.

films.title: Trainspotting (1996)
films.funding: Paid for by Channel Four Films, the film arm of the UK public-service broadcaster, and produced by Figment Films. PolyGram released it.

films.title: Akira (1988)
films.funding: Funded by the Akira Committee, a Japanese production committee of companies including publisher Kodansha, Mainichi Broadcasting, toy maker Bandai, ad agency Hakuhodo and Toho. Tokyo Movie Shinsha animated it.

films.title: An American Werewolf in London
films.funding: PolyGram Pictures financed it with The Guber-Peters Company, and Universal released it.

films.title: Donnie Darko (2001)
films.funding: An independent film financed by Pandora Cinema with Drew Barrymore's Flower Films, released in the US by Newmarket Films.

films.title: Shall We Dance? (1996)
films.funding: Backed by Nippon TV, ad agency Hakuhodo, distributor Nippon Shuppan Hanbai and the studio Daiei. Toho released it in Japan and Miramax bought it for the US.

films.title: The Return (2003)
films.funding: Zvyagintsev's debut was produced by REN Film, the Moscow company of Dmitry Lesnevsky. Shown alongside his new film Minotaur.

films.title: Hard Ticket to Hawaii
films.funding: A Sidaris family production: Andy and Arlene Sidaris made it through their own Malibu Bay Films for the video market.

films.title: Offside (2006)
films.funding: Produced by Jafar Panahi's own company and shot partly during a real qualifying match, without official backing in Iran. Sony Pictures Classics released it in the US.

films.title: Mortu Nega (1988)
studios: Instituto Nacional de Cinema da Guiné-Bissau
films.funding: Made by Guinea-Bissau's National Film Institute, the state body that produced the country's first fiction feature after independence.

films.title: Time of the Gypsies (1988)
films.funding: Produced by Forum Sarajevo with Mirza Pašić and Bond producer Harry Saltzman, and distributed by Columbia Pictures.

films.title: Near Dark (1987)
films.funding: A $5 million independent production by F/M Entertainment, distributed by the De Laurentiis Entertainment Group.

films.title: Fat City (1972) + For Mouna
films.funding: Ray Stark's Rastar produced Fat City for Columbia Pictures. The opening short For Mouna is a 2023 Belgian short by Spencer Bogaert.

films.title: De Ijzeren Reus (1999)
films.funding: The Iron Giant was made by Warner Bros. Feature Animation, the studio's in-house animation unit.

films.title: Coyote Ugly + Cocktail
films.funding: Both are Disney films released under its Touchstone label: Coyote Ugly with Jerry Bruckheimer Films, Cocktail with the investment fund Silver Screen Partners.

films.title: Damned if You Don't + Dildotectónica
films.funding: Su Friedrich makes her experimental films largely on her own. We found no funding details for the 2023 Portuguese short Dildotectónica.

films.title: Apolline + Bruges-La-Morte
films.funding: Two rarely shown adaptations, one shot in Ghent in 1959. We could not find reliable information on who financed either film.

films.title: Love That Moves the Slug
films.funding: Short-film programme curated by artist Anouk De Clercq; many different makers. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: KIDScinema: The Best of Filem'On
films.funding: Short films for children from the Filem'On festival. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: Night of the Horror: Bad Trip
match: Night of the Horror: Bad Trip
films.funding: Triple bill with Kuru: A Lizard in a Woman's Skin (1971), MadS and Brain Damage (1988). Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: Freeride Filmfestival
films.funding: Touring programme of ski and snowboard films. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: Cinéconcert voor kinderen
films.funding: Live music to short films for children, with FilemKING. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: Inmate Sessions Live!
films.funding: Cine-concert and talk about cinema in Ghent prison. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.

films.title: La Gradiva
films.funding: Les Films du Poisson (FR) with Bibi Film TV (IT). CNC €70,000 and Italy's MIC €70,000 in French-Italian co-production aid; budget unknown.

films.title: Un anno di scuola
films.funding: Nefertiti Film (IT) with Tomsa Films (FR). CNC €40,000 and Italy's MIC €60,000 in co-production aid; budget unknown.

films.title: Iron Boy (Le Corset)
films.funding: Beside Production and RTBF (BE) with Eddy Cinéma, Regular Production, France 3 and Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes Cinéma (FR). Amounts and budget unknown.

films.title: De komst van Joachim Stiller
films.funding: Majority Flemish production. Producers, funds and budget unknown.

films.title: Wild Horse Nine
films.funding: Blueprint Pictures and Film4; Searchlight Pictures distributes. Budget unknown.

films.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
match: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
films.funding: Produced by T-Street, financed by MRC. Budget unknown.

films.title: Hope
films.funding: Plus M Entertainment invests and distributes. Budget about ₩70 billion (≈ $46M), reported as Korea's most expensive film.

films.title: The Devils
films.funding: Russo Productions; Warner Bros. distributed. Budget unknown.

films.title: An Inconvenient Truth
films.funding: Participant Productions and Lawrence Bender Productions; Paramount Classics distributed. Budget $1.5M.

films.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
films.funding: Vortex Inc.; Bill Parsley's MAB Inc. put in $60,000 for 50% of the film. Budget $80,000–140,000 (sources give up to $300,000).

films.title: Near Dark
films.funding: F/M Entertainment; De Laurentiis Entertainment Group distributed. Budget $5M.

films.title: The Bibi Files
films.funding: Jigsaw Productions (Alex Gibney) with Drucker & Goren Media. Budget unknown.

films.title: Mumbo Jumbo
films.funding: A.Film A/S (DK); sales by LevelK. Funds and budget unknown.

films.title: Children of Liberty
films.funding: Folivari (FR), Tchack (BE) and Mélusine Productions (LU). Funds and budget unknown.

films.title: Coyote vs. Acme
films.funding: Warner Bros. paid the $70M production, then shelved it; Ketchup Entertainment paid $50M to release it.

films.title: Monster Mia
films.funding: arx anima (AT) with Arxlight Pictures, Ikiru Films (ES) and Peng! Boom! Tschak! (DE); sales Sola Media. Funds and budget unknown.

films.title: Resident Evil
films.funding: Columbia Pictures, Constantin Film, Davis Films, PlayStation Productions and others; Sony distributes. Budget $75M.

films.title: Yugly
films.funding: nWave Studios (Brussels). Funds and budget unknown.
